messages:
maddie: fyi customer J-Prod (tenant: jupiter-payments) opened an escalation — they see p95/p99 regressions but only on streaming endpoints. non-stream total latency looks fine. attaching their repro steps they provided.

ravi: can you paste the sample logs / request id? is this SSE or h2-streaming?

maddie: SSE. request id from their example: req_0x9a7b. they say first-chunk TTFB jumped from ~40ms p95 to ~450ms p95 over the last 12h. total completion time unchanged.

sam: adding initial triage notes: symptoms indicate first-byte delay (chunking/flush) rather than token generation. client sees delayed first chunk but subsequent tokens stream normally. suggests flush windows or proxy coalescing.

maddie: customer provided curl repro:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-small" -d '{"input":"simple prompt"}'
```
They reported 3/10 requests hit the slow TTFB case.

ravi: can you grab an edge trace for req_0x9a7b? also confirm if they hit our edge region eu-west-1 or us-east-1.

maddie: edge trace attached from customer (trimmed): "edge-hop=eu-west-1, proxy=ap-rt-2, connpool=busy, bytes-sent=0 until 450ms" (their header dump).

sam: i replicated locally against a sandbox tenant. i see the same pattern when our proxy coalesces tiny frames: server emits first chunk but it's buffered at the proxy for ~300-600ms under certain connpool conditions. hypothesis: proxy or client-side Nagle/flush interaction + our chunk size heuristic.

tanya: interesting — we changed the default flush heuristic in runtime v2.3 last month to batch tiny prefix tokens to reduce QPS. that would decrease token cost but could increase TTFB for tiny prompts. worth checking rollout windows.

ops-bot: deploy.v2.3 completed to eu-west-1 at 3055500000.

ravi: ok, plan: 1) reproduce with smallest prompt and capture tcpdump at edge, 2) try forcing smaller runtime flush window (config: streaming.min_flush_ms=0) to confirm, 3) if confirmed, advise temporary tenant override to disable batching for jupiter-payments, 4) open eng-runtime ticket for a targeted fix (adaptive flush for tiny prompts).

maddie: i've asked customer for permission to toggle tenant override. they approved. toggled streaming.min_flush_ms=0 for tenant jupiter-payments at 3055551200.

sam: after override i re-ran the curl repro from customer path — TTFB reduced to ~50-80ms p95. looks like flush/aggregation was the main factor.

ravi: can you capture metrics pre/post? want p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and total for past 24h and for the 30m after override.

maddie: pulled metrics: pre-override p95 TTFB ~420ms, p99 ~890ms. post-override p95 ~68ms, p99 ~220ms. total latency p95 unchanged at ~1.2s. attaching short CSV snippet.

tanya: thanks team. mitigation is tenant override + engineering follow-up. proposed eng-runtime action items: revert the aggressive tiny-token batching for streaming endpoints or make it request-size adaptive; add a runtime flag to disable aggregation per-route; add canary tests to detect TTFB regressions on streaming.

ravi: i'll file ENG-RT-4823 with repro steps and tcpdump + metrics. customer notified and will monitor.

maddie: customer confirmed improved UX after override. closing escalation but keeping eng ticket open until a proper fix. :thumbsup:

sam: notes for runbook: when streaming-only TTFB regression reported, check (1) recent runtime flush heuristic rollouts, (2) proxy connpool/backpressure flags, (3) tenant overrides available as immediate mitigation, (4) capture edge tcpdump + req id, (5) correlate first-byte vs total latency in metrics.

ravi: agree. adding short checklist to support KB.

maddie: thanks everyone. leaving this thread for eng owners.
